'''Johanna Liesbeth Kubelka Döbereiner''' (28 November 1924 – 5 October 2000) was a [[Brazilians|Brazilian]] [[Agronomy|agronomist]] and pioneer in soil biology.

==Biography==
Döbereiner was born in [[Ústí nad Labem]] in [[Czechoslovakia]] (now in the [[Czech Republic]]) on 28 November 1924.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Women Pioneers in Plant Biology|url=https://aspb.org/wipb-pioneer-biographies/|access-date=2020-06-04|website=American Society of Plant Biologists}}</ref> Her family were [[Germans in Czechoslovakia (1918–1938)|German Czechs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deviante.com.br/noticias/quem-foi-johanna-dobereiner/|title=Quem foi Johanna Döbereiner |date=19 June 2018 |accessdate=2019-04-19}}</ref> Her father was Professor [[Paul Kubelka]] and her mother Margarethe Kubelka. Her name Döbereiner came from her husband Jürgen Döbereiner, whom she met in [[Munich]]. Interestingly, her name became similar to the famous chemist [[Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner]], who was born in [[Hof, Bavaria]], in the border with [[Bohemia]].

Johanna Döbereiner received her degree from the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]] (LMU), but settled in Brazil and became a Brazilian citizen in 1956. Her early work includes studies of [[Azospirillum]] and other bacteria that could be useful to Brazilian soil.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mcdb.ucla.edu/Research/Hirsch/imagesb/HistoryDiscoveryN2fixingOrganisms.pdf |title=History of discovery of N2-fixing organisms, UCLA |accessdate=2012-04-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709042326/http://www.mcdb.ucla.edu/Research/Hirsch/imagesb/HistoryDiscoveryN2fixingOrganisms.pdf |archivedate=9 July 2010}}</ref> She later played an important role in Brazil's [[soybean]] production by encouraging a reliance on varieties that solely depended on [[biological nitrogen fixation]].<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CDAEZ6z0q1MC&q=%22Johanna+D%C3%B6bereiner%22&pg=PA3|title=Nitrogen Fixation: Global Perspectives : Proceedings of the 13th International Congress on Nitrogen Fixation, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, 2-7 July 2001|publisher=[[CABI (organisation)|CABI Publishing]]|page=3|chapter=Johanna Döbereiner Memorial Lecture|editor1-last=Finan |editor1-first=Turlough M. |editor2-last=O'Brian |editor2-first= Mark R.|editor3-last=Layzell |editor3-first=David B.|editor4-last=Vessey |editor4-first=J. Kevin|editor5-last=Newton |editor5-first=William|display-editors =1|last1=Baldani |first1=J.I.|last2=Baldani |first2=V.L.D.|last3=Reis |first3=V.M.|year=2002|isbn=9781845933357|display-authors =1}}</ref>

As a consequence of her research and ideas, numerous soybean plantations in Brazil are now completely supplied for nitrogen (N) by [[rhizobia]] and not using any N-fertilizers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/news/brazil-farmers-plant-legumes-as-mini-fertilizer-factories|title=Brazil farmers plant legumes as mini fertilizer factories |date=16 November 2018 |accessdate=2019-04-16}}</ref> This movement has had big benefits, because Brazil, together with the U.S., are the main producers of soybean in the world (ca. 50% world production).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-brazil-soy-usa/brazil-to-pass-u-s-as-worlds-largest-soy-producer-in-2018-idUSKBN1IC2IW |title=Brazil large soy producer |newspaper=Reuters |date=11 May 2018 |accessdate=2019-04-16}}</ref> Considering that soybeans are one of the most important global sources of protein (mainly fed to animals that in turn becomes animal protein for human consumption), this implies that significant amount of global protein comes from an ecological biological process without the use of industrial chemical fertilizers.

This was one of the reasons that Johanna Döbereiner was indicated for the [[Nobel Prize]] in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://agencia.fapesp.br/when-will-brazil-have-a-nobel/14577/ |title=When will Brazil have a Nobel Prize |accessdate=2019-04-16}}</ref>

The [[Johanna Döbereiner Biological Resources Center]] was named in her honour in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Biological resource center is inaugurated in Rio de Janeiro|url=https://www.embrapa.br/en/search-news/-/noticia/22545415/centro-de-recursos-biologicos-e-inaugurado-no-rio-de-janeiro|access-date=2020-06-04|website=embrapa.br}}</ref>
